title: The Principle of Complementarity in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum mechanics suggests that certain properties, such as wave and particle nature, cannot be observed simultaneously using a single experimental setup. The principle of complementarity posits that the description of an object in terms of its waves (wave packets) and its description in terms of particles (discrete points) are both necessary for a complete understanding. Neither aspect invalidates the other; rather, they represent different facets of the same underlying reality.

This duality implies that the experimental context dictates which property will manifest and be measurable. For example, observing the interference pattern indicates wave-like behavior, while detecting a specific impact location points to particle behavior. The inherent uncertainty in measurement prevents the simultaneous observation of all these complementary aspects with perfect accuracy.
